newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Noon Australian stocks settle at record highs.
newsitem.headline: Noon Australian stocks settle at record highs.

text.p: SPI Futures 2611 +8 US 30yr cl 6.98 -0.05
10yrbond futs 92.535 +0.100 Gold NY 345.75 Lon fix 343.90
*Stocks settle in at record levels with gains across board, option exercises boost volumes. Volume 298.37 million, A$1.31 bln value, 908 stocks traded, 321 steady, 378 up, 209 down.
The Australian share market was settling in above the 2,600 level by midday on Friday with bellwether BHP setting the pace, although rises were widespread.
By 12.00 p.m. (0200 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was up 16.3 points at a record high of 2,606.9, surpassing Thursday's previous record high of 2,591.5.
June share price index futures were eight points higher at 2,611, a 4.1 point premium to the underlying index.
May series option exercises after Thursday's expiry boosted volumes, with over A$993 million in turnover put through prior to the market opening.
"It's generally been pretty good," said dealer Mark Pervan of Daiwa Securities, pointing to strength in the bond market and market leader BHP as key drivers in the strong showing.
"The bond market looks good and BHP is recovering as well."
BHP climbed 1.8 percent to A$18.93 but all the leaders showed solid gains, aided by the resetting of positions after Thursday's May series option expiries.

Weaker than expected April retail sales figures had little impact, with moves in the sector only marginal. "The retail figure was a little bit surprising but it didn't have a reaction in the retail sector. They held up pretty well," Pervan said.

Ongoing action in the second tier oils was noted, with Cultus Petroleum again strongly sought after Thursday's reserve estimate upgrade at the Cornea oil field offshore Western Australia. Cultus shares added five percent to A$3.96, while Novus Petroleum was the best of the rest, adding 1.7 percent to a record high A$4.83, albeit on lighter trade.
"Interest just continues in the oil sector with the new players there," Pervan said.
Chemicals group ICI Australia added nine cents to A$12.20 after anouncing a buyback of A$360 million worth of its parent ICI Plc's stake.
ANZ Bank was the strongest performer in that sector, adding 1.8 percent to A$8.89, while sector leader National Australia Bank climbed one percent to A$18.75.

Among the building materials, Boral was the star of the show, climbing 2.7 percent to A$4.20, but others also turned in impressive gains. Pioneer International added 1.6 percent to A$4.51 while CSR rose 1.7 percent to A$4.86.
CSR earlier announced the sale of its American Aggregates business for about A$345 million.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about nine to five, while about 35 percent of stocks traded remained steady.

In other local markets, Australian debt futures surged after retail trade fell for the second consecutive month in April, fuelling speculation that last Friday's official rate cut to 5.5 percent may not be the last this cycle.
By 1.00 p.m. (0300 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.46 percent, compared to Thursday's 7.57 percent.

The Australian dollar dived over 1/2 cent at the midsession as a fledgling rally was cruelly undermined by shockingly weak retail trade data. By 1.00 p.m. (0300 GMT) the local dollar had crumbled to US$0.7622/27 from US$0.7680/85 just before the data hit dealing screens and US$0.7658/63 late here Thursday.
